_comment: Every behaviour this tree promises to change at the next major.
A staged flip is a promise made to a user now about a release that has not
happened: `This becomes an error in 6.0.0.` is printed on stderr today by
code that still allows the thing. This file is the register of those
promises; `docs/governance/V6_0_PLAN.md` holds the reasoning, the gate
conditions and the open decisions.
`nodus_gate --flips` checks that this file and `src/` agree, in both
directions. It exists because they did not: five promises lived in src/
while COMPATIBILITY_MODEL.md said three, COMPATIBILITY.md said one, and a
design doc said a fourth had been dropped. The two that went missing were
the two whose issues had been closed -- the staging shipped, the issue
closed, and the flip fell out of every register while the code kept
promising it.
Each site in src/ carries a `# v6-flip: <name>` marker, the same way a
regression test carries `# closes: #N`. Attribution needs it: two of these
flips live in one file and their promise text is nearly identical.
`signal` is not decoration. COMPATIBILITY_MODEL.md 5.1 makes a CLI warning
one of three required deprecation signals, and two entries here do not have
one -- which is a fact about whether the flip may be taken, so it belongs
next to the flip.

rebuild-effect.summary: A rebuild that re-runs a top-level effect refuses it instead of repeating it
rebuild-effect.why_check: `nodus check` warns rather than errs: the refusal happens only when a stored run is resumed, so a program that is never resumed runs correctly.
rebuild-effect.override: NODUS_REBUILD_EFFECTS=allow, or rebuild_effects="allow" on sweep/new_vm, for a run whose stored source predates its fix

worker-dispatcher.summary: A `worker:` declaration with no registered dispatcher is refused instead of running in-process
worker-dispatcher.why_check: `nodus check` warns rather than errs: whether a dispatcher is registered is a deployment fact the source cannot see.

library-run-loop.summary: `run_loop()` called from library code (any module but the program's entry file) is refused
library-run-loop.why_check: `nodus check` errs: the scan is exact. A run_loop() call in an imported file is library code wherever it is, and fails whenever it runs.

concurrent-write.summary: A concurrent state write that loses an update is refused instead of warned about
concurrent-write.why_check: `nodus check` warns rather than errs: the static answer is a superset. It reports every unordered pair of writers, and whether one update is lost depends on the values and the interleaving at run time.

unknown-type-name.summary: An unrecognised type name is a syntax error instead of meaning `any`
unknown-type-name.why_check: No separate scan: the parser itself refuses the name, so `nodus check`, `nodus run` and the LSP all report it as a syntax error at its token.

record-equality.summary: Record `==` compares by value (kind and fields) instead of identity
record-equality.why_check: No scan: whether a comparison's answer changed depends on the runtime type of both `==` operands, which the source cannot see. The change only makes `==` true where it was false for two distinct records with equal fields.

default-store-sqlite.summary: The default workflow store becomes SQLiteWorkflowStore
default-store-sqlite.signal: ok as of the G2 work -- a StagedFlipWarning, which the CLI unsuppresses and renders as `warning: ...`; it was a plain DeprecationWarning raised outside __main__ and no CLI user had ever seen it
default-store-sqlite.why: The only flip in the cohort that costs state rather than a build: runs in the JSON store are invisible to a SQLite one, so an in-flight waiting run becomes unresumable rather than moving. `nodus workflow migrate-store --to sqlite` is the migration. **The flip lands as a refusal, not a silent switch** -- as of the stranded-runs check, opting into SQLite while the JSON store holds unmigrated runs warns and names them, and at 6.0.0 that becomes an error. That is what makes the switch safe to take: the harm this flip needed a long deprecation clock for was that it failed silently.
